The prosperity of the various African companies for nearly four centuries depended in large measure on the slave trade. Its suppression in the nineteenth century

positions.title: coinciding with the Ashanti wars,  reduced commerce on the coast to straits from which it revived only temporarily when the security of Captain Maclean's administration fostered the development of the palm oil trade. Vegetable oils remained for several decades one of the principal objects of commerce on the coast. This and other trades were,  however,  displaced in importance by the cocoa industry which from small beginnings rapidly expanded in the new century until the Gold Coast became the world's largest producer,  and cocoa the key to the country's prosperity. This prosperity is being threatened by swollen shoot,  a serious and contagious virus disease of cocoa whose depredations constitute a grave menace to the economy of the country. A strenuous campaign based on the best scientific advice and research is being waged by Government and slow but steady progress is being made in the eradication of the diseased trees and the rehabilitation of the devastated areas. The marketing of cocoa has been undertaken since 1947 by the Government sponsored Gold Coast Cocoa Marketing Board.

positions.title: 1951,  which came into operation on 31st August,  1951,  the Legislative Council was reconstituted; it now consists of the Administrator as President,  two other ex-officio members (the Attorney General and Treasurer) three nominated members (being persons not holding a public office in the Colony) and eight elected members (one for each of eight electoral districts) elected by universal adult suffrage. Property and income qualifications of candidates for elected membership were abolished. The Governor may address the Council at any time he thinks fit. No change was made in the Governor’s reserve powers. At the same time the Executive Council was reconstituted by Royal Instructions; it now consists of the Administrator,  if the Governor is present in the Executive Council,  and two other ex-officio members (the persons who are ex-officio members of the Legislative Council),  one official member appointed by the Governor,  who must be a person holding a public office in the Colony,  one nominated member appointed by the Governor from among the nominated members of the Legislative Council,  and three elected members who are elected by the Legislative Council from among the elected members of that Council.

people.name: During 1950 and early 1951 a review of the machinery for inter-territorial consultation in West Africa was carried out

positions.title: particular regard being paid to the recent and impending constitutional changes in West Africa which made it desirable that Africans should take a greater part in inter-territorial consultation and collaboration. As a result the Secretary of State (Mr. James Griffiths) announced on the 30th May,  1951,  the dissolution of the West African Council and the setting up in its place of the West African Inter-Territorial Conference. The Conference,  which will meet at least once a year and which will hold its first meeting in 1952,  consists of two members of the Executive Council (or Council of Ministers) from each British West African territory,  nominated by the Governor-in-Council. The Chairman of the Conference is the Governor of Nigeria or,  in his absence,  a deputy nominated by him after consultation with the other Governors. The functions of the Conference are as follows:

people.name: His Late Majesty the King approved in principle recommendations which had been made by the High Commissioner for the Western Pacific for the separation of the office of High Commissioner from that of Governor of Fiji

positions.title: and for the creation of a new post,  the duties of which would include administration of the Gilbert and Ellice Islands Colony and the British Solomon Islands Protectorate. The High Commissioner for the Western Pacific would continue to be the British High Commissioner for the New Hebrides Condominium. It is proposed that these recommendations shall become effective on the retirement from the Service of the present Governor and High Commissioner,  Sir Leslie Brian Freeston,  K.C.M.G.,  O.B.E.,  early in 1952. The headquarters of the new administration will be moved to the British Solomon Islands Protectorate when the necessary buildings have been erected.
